about: Balanced-ternary packed weights library — P2 runtime format (4 trits/byte, code=t+1 in 2 bits), P3 storage/network format (5 trits/byte base-3), and L5 lookup-table compute (P3 code as 243-entry table index). Emitted as cpp/trit.hpp (header-only) and rust crate (no_std core, AVX2-gated kernels) from a single Omniglyph multilingual spec (TRIT-LIB-3, cohort lock phase).

P2.description: Runtime format: 4 trits/byte, code = trit+1 mapped to 2 bits; row bytes = ((n+31)/32)*8; AVX2 unpack via shuffle+mask+compare; dot = exact sign_epi8 dot product with scalar tail

P3.description: Storage/network format: 5 trits/byte base-3 (3^5=243 <= 256); decoded by 243-entry static table (int8[243][5]); pack computes code = low_digit + 3*mid + 9*... + 81*high

L5.description: Compute directly on P3 storage form (P3 code as 243-entry LUT index); 16 queries at once; int16 lane accumulators widened to int32 per L5_KCH=4 blocks; 2-D tiled: L2-sized 124KB table chunk x L1-sized 512-row acc tiles. Exact vs scalar reference (0 mismatches, verified). Note: rust crate includes scalar L5 reference (l5::reference) and P3 table (P3Table); C++ L5 in header (l5_pack, l5_build16, l5_gemm16) is full AVX2 kernel.

laws.statement: P2 packs 4 trits/byte: code = trit+1 in 2 bits, row padded to multiple of 32 trits, bytes/row = ((n+31)/32)*8

forms.rust: pub fn row_bytes(n: usize) -> usize { n.div_ceil(32) * 8 }

laws.statement: P2 pack_row writes code=t+1 into 2-bit slots of each packed byte; zero-padded with code 1 (t=0); row bytes pre-filled with 0x55 (four zero trits)

laws.statement: P2 pack produces a vector of packed bytes (4 trits/byte); exact inverse of unpack via AVX2 unpack32 + scalar tail; verified 0 mismatches vs int8 scalar dot on all test shapes (1,31,32,33,100,129,C) at R=8192 C=4096

laws.statement: P2 unpack32: 8 packed bytes -> 32 int8 trits in one AVX2 register (shuffle + mask + compare + sub from two); exact (bit-identical to scalar)
laws.assume: p points to at least 8 packed bytes; AVX2 enabled

laws.statement: P2 dot = AVX2 sign_epi8 dot (32-wide batches) + scalar tail (per-byte shift/mask); exact vs scalar reference on all shapes; 0 mismatches verified via trit_pack_test.cpp (R=8192, C=4096, 1..4 threads)
laws.assume: x[i] in [-128,127]; p = p2_pack(W); n multiple of 32 preferred (tail handled)

laws.statement: P2 dot4 computes 4 rows at once: one int8 activation load reused across 4 weight rows; exact same sums as 4*p2_dot; exactness: bad4 = 0 on all sampled rows (verified by trit_pack_test.cpp)
laws.assume: 4 rows contiguous in packed memory; AVX2 enabled

laws.statement: P3 storage: 5 trits/byte; base-3 encoding: 3^5=243 <= 256; each byte = low_digit + 3*d2 + 9*d3 + 27*d4 + 81*d5; decode via 243-entry static table P3Table::new() (const, no_std)
laws.assume: t[i] in {-1,0,+1}; n any positive integer

laws.statement: P3 pack produces base-3 byte codes from int8 trits (-1->0, 0->1, +1->2); exact round-trip verified (back == W) by trit_pack_test.cpp; static P3Table decodes 243 codes to 5 int8 trits

laws.statement: P3 unpack uses static P3Table (243 entries x 5 int8) to decode each byte back to 5 trits; exact round-trip verified; no_std compatible (static const)
laws.assume: P3 bytes produced by p3_pack; n matches original

laws.statement: L5: compute directly on P3 storage codes (each 5-trit group = 243-entry index); 16 queries at once (int16 lanes); int16 sums widened to int32 every L5_KCH=4 blocks to stay within int16 bound (<32767); 2-D tiled: 124KB L2 table chunks x 512-row L1 accumulators; exact vs scalar reference (0 mismatches) at odd widths, nq=1/7/16, x <= -127, n=1..129,C
laws.assume: P3 codes in [0,242]; x in [-128,127] (absmax quant limits); n padded to multiple of 20; nq <= 16

forms.c: constexpr int L5_KCH = 4, L5_RT = 512; inline int l5_blocks(int n) { return (n + 19) / 20; } ... inline void l5_gemm16(...) { ... } ... inline std::vector<uint8_t> l5_pack(...) { ... } ... inline void l5_build16(...) { ... }
forms.rust: pub const L5_KCH: usize = 4; pub const L5_RT: usize = 512; pub mod l5 { ... }

laws.statement: L5 gemm: 16-query batch over P3 packed weights (L5_pack); per-query x loaded as int8 lanes; 243-entry partial-sum tables built per 5-input chunk (len *= 3 each digit); 4-block (KCH=4) chunks => 124KB table (fits L2); 512-row tiles (L5_RT) keep accumulators in L1; exact vs scalar reference (0 mismatches at all shapes)
laws.assume: L = l5_pack(W); X16 = 16 query vectors; nq <= 16; n padded to multiple of 20; AVX2 enabled
